Is your child waiting for the third ask? 🔊 One day that habit could cost more than an open door.

Sadie is five. Every day the pattern gets built: "Sadie, close the door." Nothing. "Sadie… the DOOR." Nothing. "SADIE!" Now she moves. 🚪

Mom has three voices: practice, warning and real. And Sadie has tuned her ears to number three. 🎚️

Then one day it matters. Outside the grocery store, her ball rolls toward the road. "Sadie, stop." But it's not the loud voice yet… 🛑 Sadie is safe. But Mom cries the whole way home.

So Mom changes the pattern:
1️⃣ Get close.
2️⃣ Eyes first. One small study found children followed instructions better when the adult made eye contact first. 👀
3️⃣ Say it once.
4️⃣ Pause.
If she starts, "Thank you!" If she doesn't, it ends in calm action. No lecture.

"So shall my word be that goes out from my mouth; it shall not return to me empty, but it shall accomplish that which I purpose." Isaiah 55:11 (ESV) 🙏 God's word works, and Jesus proved it on the cross.

Months later, the ball bounces toward the road again. "Sadie, stop." And she stops. ❤️ The first word might be the one that matters most.
